text:
Nina P: Hi all — quick newbie question. I copied our docker-compose.yml and set network_mode: host on the db service because I wanted the app to reach Postgres on localhost. Now the db container exits immediately with: "service "db" uses the host network driver, which is not supported on Mac/Colima" and my app still can't connect. Also Redis keeps rejecting with ERR NOAUTH even though I put REDIS_PASSWORD in .env. Any straightforward fixes?

Ethan: welcome! network_mode: host is a Linux-only thing — it won't work on macOS Docker/Colima. Remove that and use the default bridge network or service hostnames. In compose your app should connect to host: db (the service name) on port 5432.

Ethan: Example: in app env `DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@db:5432/appdb` and in compose both services on the same network.

Olga: If you need to connect from your host machine (outside containers) to the Postgres running in compose, map the port: `ports: - "5432:5432"` on the db service. But avoid host networking in compose for mac.

Nina P: Ah that makes sense. I had assumed host mode would expose it to my host. I removed network_mode and used the service name; db starts now. One follow-up: when I map ports 5432:5432 I sometimes get "address already in use" because I have a local postgres installed. How do people handle that?

Priya N: Two approaches: (1) stop the local postgres service while using the compose db; (2) map to a different host port like `55432:5432` and point your host-side tools to localhost:55432. We usually use a nonstandard host port to avoid conflicts.

Olga: about the Redis NOAUTH: double-check which redis container you're hitting. If you have two compose files or an old named container, your app might be talking to the wrong one. Run `docker ps` and `docker-compose ps` to confirm. Also verify the redis service actually got the env var: `docker-compose exec redis env | grep REDIS_PASSWORD`.

Nina P: I ran `docker ps` and saw an older `project_redis_1` container from a prior compose run. Stopped and removed it and now the app auth works. Thanks!

infra-bot: dev-runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/local-db-setup 1: see section "Networking differences on macOS/Colima" and "Port conflicts & host tools" for recommended patterns.

Priya N: quick checklist for the thread: 1) remove network_mode: host on mac, 2) use service hostnames between containers, 3) map ports only if host access needed and avoid conflicts by using alternate host ports, 4) ensure env file is picked up (check `docker-compose --env-file` if needed), 5) prune old containers with `docker-compose down -v` if stale.

Nina P: Following the checklist fixed my problems. Appreciate the quick help :tada:
